Inland Express

Some bold artistic choices - that by the looks of it are really not for everyone, but I love it. This captures the fever dream, hypnotic vampirism I always expected from the legend, only in this grainy modern noir coat. Some elements are a little out of place - "psychic fax", and Van Helsing giving 'Doc Brown' vibes - but despite that this is now one of my favourite vampire films.

Did I enjoy a single minute of this film?... No, not really

This is Herzog at his 'best' and absolute worst; Conceptually this has potential to be a fantastically fun and surreal commentary, told through a fever dream of a film. However, the lack of meaningful story moments and the numerous yet casual animal abuses throughout makes it impossible for me to appreciate this film in any real way.

Everything you'd expect from a Tarchovsky Sci-fi, it's a slow yet artfully done story, symbolism through nature, amazing sets and score, etc. It's a film that demands multiple watches to appreciate all it's aspects.

But I have to say that this film was slightly tougher to get through than, say, Stalker. The story is one that on face value doesn't seem that special, but there may be a truly amazing story between the lines that I didn't quite connect with on my first watch. In this sense my initial thoughts are that this film is a touch overrated.
